questions.q: Why does the capstone build three groups for Lakeview Facilities instead of assigning roles to 40 individual users?
options: Groups don't actually support role assignment in ServiceNow
Role inheritance through group membership stays manageable as people join or leave, instead of editing 40 individual user records
Individual role assignment is required by ServiceNow for compliance reasons
Groups are only used for notifications, never for roles
questions.explain: Chapter 1's pattern is to build group structure first and let inherited roles follow group membership, which scales far better than per-user role edits.

questions.q: Why is a UI Policy alone not sufficient to protect the estimated_cost field from staff?
options: A UI Policy is client-side only and doesn't stop a report, Import Set, or integration from exposing the field
UI Policies cannot be applied to currency fields
UI Policies only work on the Service Catalog, not on custom tables
A UI Policy would delete the field entirely
questions.explain: Lesson 22 established that UI Policies are presentation-layer only — real enforcement against any access path requires a field-level ACL.

questions.q: What correctly scopes the field-level ACL on estimated_cost in this scenario?
options: A table-level ACL on the entire Facilities Request table requiring no role
A field-level ACL on estimated_cost requiring the facilities_coordinator role for both read and write
No ACL — the UI Policy is sufficient
A field-level ACL that only restricts write access, leaving read open to everyone
questions.explain: Both read and write need the coordinator role, enforced at the data layer, so the field is invisible and unwritable to staff regardless of how it's accessed.

questions.q: Why does the Furniture Request catalog item use a catalog UI policy to make 'current item' mandatory only for Replacement or Relocation requests?
options: A brand-new furniture request (New Item) has no existing item to describe, so the field shouldn't be forced there
Catalog UI policies can only apply to mandatory fields
The field should always be mandatory regardless of request type
Catalog UI policies are unrelated to variable sets
questions.explain: Making the field conditionally mandatory matches the real logic of the request type — there's nothing to describe on a New Item request.

questions.q: Why is the fulfillment notification built as condition-based (state changes to Closed Complete) rather than event-based?
options: Event-based notifications don't exist in ServiceNow
A simple field-change condition already captures exactly the one state transition that matters, with no need for a custom scripted event
Condition-based notifications cannot use email templates
Event-based notifications are always a better choice for every scenario
questions.explain: Lesson 16 distinguished the two trigger types — this scenario's need is fully met by a straightforward condition, so a custom event would be unnecessary complexity.
